newsitem.title: UK: Sun sets on Webber's Boulevard in London.
newsitem.headline: Sun sets on Webber's Boulevard in London.

text.p: Sunset Boulevard, Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber's musical version of the tale of an ageing Hollywood screen star, will close in April, producers said on Sunday.
The curtain will fall on the 4.5 million pound ($7 million) blockbuster because producers cannot find a big enough star to replace singer Petula Clark in the leading role.
Based on the 1950s Billy Wilder film of the same name, Sunset Boulevard has been seen by nearly two million people in London since it opened in July 1993 with Patti LuPone playing Norma Desmond.

"Sir Andrew Lloyd Webber has scripted one of the most demanding female roles ever in musical theatre. This makes casting incredibly difficult," James Thane, managing director of the Really Useful Theatre Company, said.
"The public expect a certain stature of artist in this role and to continue beyond Petula's contract would risk compromising an extraordinary series of bravura performances."
Betty Buckley, Elaine Paige and Rita Moreno have also starred in the London production of the musical. Glenn Close opened the Los Angeles version in 1993.

In 1994 Lloyd Webber decided to close in Los Angeles rather than proceed with actress Faye Dunaway in the leading role. He said Dunaway's singing was not good enough. Dunaway sued, but finally settled out of court. The Broadway version, which currently stars Elaine Paige, is to close on March 22. ($1=.6237 Pound)
